messages.subject: RPostgreSQL and sqldf?
messages.body_plain:
According to the comments on http://blog.chrischou.org/2010/09/28/play-sqldf-with-rpostgresql/
RPostgreSQL does not provide capabilities needed to use it as a driver
for library( sqldf).  Has anyone investigated this?  I could not get
the RpgSQL driver, which is JDBC at its core, to authenticate, but
RPostgreSQL was a snap.  sqldf looks like a lot of fun, but I can't
get it to play with my data source.  I ran this by Dirk and he asked
me to post to the group.  Thanks for any comments.


Neil

Huh?

   R> library(RPostgreSQL)
   Loading required package: DBI
   R> drv <- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")
   R> con <- dbConnect(drv, dbname="beancounter")
   R> dat <- dbGetQuery(con, "select distinct date from fxprices where date >= '2011-02-01' order by date")
   R> dat
           date
   1 2011-02-01
   2 2011-02-02
   3 2011-02-03
   4 2011-02-04
   5 2011-02-07
   R> class(dat)
   [1] "data.frame"
   R> class(dat[,"date"])
   [1] "Date"
   R> dbDisconnect(con)
   [1] TRUE
   R> dbUnloadDriver(drv)
   [1] TRUE
   R> 

Looks like Date to me.  RPostgreSQL has support Date and Datetime since the
initial GSoC project.

Dirk

| > | of support for important R classes such as "Date" and the developer of
| > | PostgreSQL did not think that such support would be available soon
| > | when I asked.
| >
| >
| > Huh?
| >
| 
| The problem you are referring to was in the RJDBC interface that
| RpgSQL  (an alternate PostgreSQL interface) uses and not in
| RPostgreSQL.

Some people are talking past each other here.  Neil started this AFAICT with
an inquiry as to why sqldf cannot / will not support RPostgreSQL.  Are you
interested in getting back to that?

I am not a user of sqldf so I don't care either way.  I got interested when
you seemingly perpetrated a completely false statement about RPostgreSQL when
I saw fit to correct. 

| The problems in RPostgreSQL itself were:
| 
| 1. in RPostgreSQL dbWriteTable writes the data frame out as a text
| file from R and then tries to read it into PostgreSQL using the
| PostgreSQL command: COPY tablename FROM 'filepath'.  In addition to
| the lack of preservation of representation and speed problems I was
| getting permission errors from the database when it tries to read the
| file.
| 
| 2. I was told that fixing the above was not expected any time soon,
| that RPostgreSQL was not currently being maintained and that it had
| not been tested on Windows.
| 
| The above problems were about a year ago, which is when I tried RPostgreSQL.

A *lot* of things have changed in the last year, but I don't think it is
worth my while enumerating them to you.   Feel free to look at the ChangeLog
if you really care.

FWIW your misinformation with respect to the lack of Date class is not
addressed by 1) or 2) above.

I am done with this thread now.

Dirk
